comments.text:
It's,  8:00 pm in Memphis, Tennessee.

I visited Sierra Leone, in  2013.  I took  pictures of the  famous Cotton Tree, which is near the ferry dock, which  takes you across the bay to the airport. 

I was told the story of the Black Americans, who fought for the British in  America's revolutionary war & was brought to the Freetown colony by way of Nova Scotia, around 1792.

Beautiful country with friendly people.  I was residing near the Congo Crossing in Freetown.

replies.author: @moewilliams6426
replies.text:
​@BestTravelDocumentary4k Our visit was great, because we had made relationships with some locals there before coming.

So, we got the chance to explore some exciting things about the country that the average visitor may not have experienced.

We visited Bo city & kenema. We ate the native dishes like, peanut stew & a dish with baked chicken, rice & veggies ; dranked palm wine & were told some interesting folklore .

Our hotel sat at the edge of the bay in Freetown & you could see the other side of the bay where the airport was located.

We caught the water taxi on arrival, but took the ferry when leaving.

Great memories.

Speaking in a normal spoken language will make the viewers understand the country and people better , rather than giving a poetic monotonous narration
